record.paper_title: Bounded compact and dual compact approximation properties of Hardy spaces: new results and open problems
record.original_question: Determine the exact value of M(H^p), the bounded compact approximation constant of the Hardy space H^p, for every 1 ≤ p < ∞.

evidence.quote: Open problem 5.5. (a) Find the exact value of M(Hp), 1 ≤ p < ∞.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $1\le p<\infty$ and let $H^p$ denote the classical Hardy space on the unit disk, namely the closed subspace of $L^p(\mathbb{T})$ (with $\mathbb{T}$ the unit circle equipped with normalized Lebesgue measure) consisting of those functions whose Fourier coefficients of negative index vanish. A Banach space $X$ is said to have the bounded compact approximation property (BCAP) with constant $C$ if there exists a net (or sequence, when $X$ is separable) of compact operators $K_\alpha\colon X\to X$ with $\sup_\alpha\|K_\alpha\|\le C$ such that $K_\alpha x\to x$ for every $x\in X$. Define
$$M(X) := \inf\{C\ge 1 : X \text{ has the BCAP with constant } C\},$$
with the convention $M(X)=\infty$ if $X$ does not have the BCAP. Determine the exact value of $M(H^p)$ for every $1\le p<\infty$.
artifact.status_search_result: The best known upper bound in the literature is $M(H^p)\le 2|1-2/p|$ for $1<p<\infty$ (with $M(H^p)\le 2$ in general), established in work by Karlovych and Shargorodsky (Indagationes Mathematicae, 2024). No matching lower bound or exact determination of $M(H^p)$ appears to be known, and the problem is explicitly listed as an open problem in that line of research.

status_evidence.title: Bounded compact and dual compact approximation properties of Hardy spaces
status_evidence.snippet: M(H^p(w)) ≤ 2|1−2/p| for 1<p<∞; the exact value of M(H^p) is posed as an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: Only upper bounds for M(H^p) are known; exact value remains open.
